scope: U.S. Census March 2026 HTOPS official direct-burden workbook map
purpose: Resolve the remaining official-source discovery gap for household burden. The official Census table locations are now known for food sufficiency, energy spending, expense difficulty, price stress, and transportation sufficiency, with corresponding standard-error tables. Numeric values are not promoted until the official workbooks are directly extracted and preserved.
sample_context: Census reports about 136,000 households for the March 2026 table release.

official_tables.title: Food Sufficiency for Households in the Last Seven Days, by Select Characteristics
Household Energy Use and Spending in the Last Two Months, by Select Characteristics
Difficulty Paying Usual Household Expenses in the Last Two Months, by Select Characteristics
Stress Caused by Price Increases, by Select Characteristics
Sufficiency of Access to Transportation During the Last Four Weeks, by Select Characteristics

governing_rules: Official workbook discovery is not equivalent to numeric custody.
Secondary reconstructions remain triangulation only until official workbook values are extracted and reconciled with the matching standard errors and table specifications.
Food insufficiency must remain distinct from enough food but not always the kinds wanted.
Expense difficulty must preserve denominator, population, and response-category construction.
Transportation insufficiency cannot be attributed to price without reason-specific evidence.
Energy spending must not be collapsed into electricity commodity price because usage, delivery, fuel choice, geography, and contract structure differ.
